hook: New books preserve 144 names after a village lost its future in seconds.

sections.voiceover: New books preserve 144 names after a village lost its future in seconds.
sections.visual_cue: Close up shot of heavy leather bound archive pages resting on a dark wooden table in an archive room.
sections.sfx_cue: Subtle low ambient tone with paper rustling
b_roll: National Library of Wales archive room overview shot

sections.voiceover: On 21 October 1966, a massive coal waste tip collapsed onto Aberfan. 116 children and 28 adults lost their lives in the disaster. Will the National Library of Wales protect these pages?
sections.visual_cue: Archival photograph of the village hillside showing the slide scar above houses.

sections.voiceover: Time wears down the original Aberfan Book of Remembrance, but fresh copies are needed.
sections.visual_cue: Extreme macro shot of aged handwriting and ink texture on a historical manuscript page.
b_roll: Macro shots of historic book bindings

sections.voiceover: The National Library of Wales finished new copies ahead of July 2026. Aberfan Memorial Charity chair Davies guards the community's history now. At 68 years old, Davies protects the village's memory.
sections.visual_cue: Modern bookbinder carefully pressing fresh gold foil lettering onto a dark memorial cover.
sections.sfx_cue: Foley of careful bookbinding tool work
b_roll: National Library of Wales bindery workshop
sections.animation_cue: pan across newly bound memorial cover

sections.voiceover: 144 names remain protected in fresh leather and ink.
sections.visual_cue: Open book showing clean memorial pages resting under soft archive desk lamps.
b_roll: Open Aberfan Book of Remembrance pages
sections.animation_cue: slow push in on inscribed names
